subject: RFI: VPC fencing, egress controls, and isolation evidence for CedarPoint Health
messages:
From: Helen Park <helen.park@cedarpointhealth.com>
To: priya.natarajan@redwood.ai, vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: security@cedarpointhealth.com
Date: Fri, 01 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Initial RFI: VPC fencing, egress controls, and isolation evidence

Priya / team,

Thanks for the quick sync yesterday. As part of our procurement we need a short evidence packet covering network isolation and egress controls for Redwood's hosted and dedicated offerings. Can you provide the following by EOD Tuesday?

- Network diagram (VPC/subnet-level) that shows tenant separation, control plane connectivity, and egress gateways.
- Explicit egress IP ranges or a published feed we can use for allowlisting (hosted and dedicated).
- Short threat model summary addressing: cross-tenant lateral movement, ingress control, and third-party integrations.
- KMS/HSM usage: what is customer-managed vs Redwood-managed, and how keys are used for model artifacts/tokenization if applicable.
- Audit/logging destinations and retention guarantees (for deployment evidence).

We will attach this to our security review. If you have a one-page runbook for incident/egress compromise, please include that as well.

Best,
Helen Park
Head of Information Security
CedarPoint Health
From: Priya Natarajan <priya.natarajan@redwood.ai>
To: Helen Park <helen.park@cedarpointhealth.com>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, karthik.iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Sat, 02 Oct 2026 10:04:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Initial RFI: VPC fencing, egress controls, and isolation evidence

Helen —

Thanks for the clear list. Attached are the artifacts you requested: redwood_vpc_fencing_diagram_v1.png (diagram), egress_controls_matrix.csv (ranges and publishing cadence), and redwood_deployment_threat_summary.pdf (concise threat model + mitigations). Highlights below:

1) Topology & isolation (diagram attached)
- Hosted API: multi-tenant in our managed VPCs; strong tenant fencing via per-request logical tenancy, mTLS for control-plane calls, and strict ACLs at the service mesh boundary.
- Dedicated: single-tenant VPCs (customer-dedicated AWS accounts or VPCs in customer cloud) with an optional private control plane tunnel.
- Private (VPC/on-prem): customer-managed network; Redwood agents run inside customer environment with no outbound to Redwood other than explicit telemetry endpoints if enabled.

2) Egress controls
- Hosted: we publish an allowlist feed (see egress_controls_matrix.csv) refreshed weekly; ranges are owned by Redwood egress gateways.
- Dedicated: by default, egress is via customer-managed NAT/GW. For Redwood-managed dedicated fleets we provide static egress CIDRs per contract (listed in the CSV).
- Private: no outbound egress unless customer enables; if enabled, IPs are customer-controlled.

3) KMS / key ownership
- Customer-managed keys (CMK) supported for model artifact encryption at rest and for encrypting customer payload tokens. We integrate with AWS KMS, GCP KMS, and Azure Key Vault.
- HSM: we offer HSM-backed key wrapping for enterprise customers (bring-your-own HSM supported for Private and Dedicated).

4) Audit & logging
- Control-plane and audit logs captured and can be exported to customer-owned S3/GCS buckets or pushed to SIEM via customer connectors. Default retention 90 days; extended retention available as a paid add-on.

5) Threat model summary (attached)
- We enumerate attack paths (egress compromise, sidecar compromise, KV cache poisoning) and controls (least privilege, network ACLs, per-request auth, runtime sandboxing, automatic fallback to model variants). See attached PDF for the matrix and evidence links.

6) Runbook
- We included a 1-page runbook excerpt in the PDF that outlines containment steps, egress disabling, and required contacts.

If you need explicit CIDRs for a contract-bound Dedicated instance, we can provide a signed addendum with static egress ranges — that requires legal/ops to approve the attachment.

Regards,

--
Priya Natarajan
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
priya.natarajan@redwood.ai

Thanks Priya — the packet looks good. A few clarifications before we sign off with procurement:

- Cross-tenant traffic: please confirm if any internal service-to-service communication may traverse other tenants for caching or KV purposes.
- Please attach the signed runbook excerpt (we can use it in our incident plan).

Attaching: security_questionnaire_v3.xlsx with a few cells pre-filled.

Best,
Helen

Helen —

Appreciate the quick turnaround. Below are the explicit answers and the static egress blocks we can provide for Redwood-managed Dedicated fleets under a standard addendum. I have also uploaded an updated CSV with the CIDRs and a signed runbook excerpt to the drive link at the bottom.

- Static egress CIDRs (Redwood-managed Dedicated):
  - 52.203.16.0/22
  - 18.197.64.0/22
  - 34.120.128.0/22
  These are the public egress ranges we will announce once the addendum is executed. They map to our managed egress gateway fleet and are reserved for dedicated contract use.

- Bastion / operator access:
  - For Redwood-managed Dedicated we require operator access through a bastionless model by default: operators authenticate via our control plane with short-lived certs and role-based access; interactive access is audited and session-recorded.
  - Customer-managed bastions are supported if requested; that configuration will be documented in the SOW and requires transport-level VPN or private peering.

- Cross-tenant traffic:
  - No cross-tenant application-level traffic occurs. Caching and KV stores are per-tenant or per-dedicated-pool; there is strict namespace separation and KMS-bound keys by tenancy. Shared telemetry pipelines are logically separated and scrubbed of tenant identifiers.

- Runbook & evidence:
  - The signed runbook excerpt and updated diagram (redwood_vpc_fencing_diagram_v2.png) are in the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcdExample
  - Egress CIDR CSV (redwood_egress_controls_matrix.csv) updated and attached.

If you want a short walk-through with our infra ops lead to validate the CIDRs and the runbook we can book 30 minutes this week — propose Wed 10/07 at 11:00 AM PT or Thu 10/08 at 2:00 PM PT.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

Best regards,
